CROSS-CUTTING CLASS 4, found in this lens and not named by the re-review: the workload-count and policy-count pair was readable as a balancing identity, and both halves fail. Interrogated and measured - (a) a non-zero policy count clears nothing: a NetworkPolicy is namespaced and selects pods by label, so two policies aimed at one front-end balance the count over a third workload that nothing selects, and a policy with an empty podSelector and an ingress rule carrying no from selector is an explicit allow-all that counts as enforcement and enforces nothing. Built the fixture: 3 workloads, 2 policies both targeting ns-a/api, ns-b/records selected by nothing, and the check does not fire. (b) a matching line is not an instance: rg -c counts lines, so several documents in one ---separated file count several times (measured: 3), a Helm template inside a range counts once and renders many (measured: 1), and a Kustomize base plus overlays counts one workload twice - so the numbers diverge on correct trees and match on broken ones. Both halves written into item 8 as an explicit read-these-as-lists-never-as-a-subtraction rule, and the severity row now states that only zero across all eight kinds is mechanical
